I'm planning on picking up a Smith and Wesson M+P Bodyguard 380ACP and can't decide whether to get the model with the integral laser sight. I thought it might be worth discussing the merits of lasers on concealed carry guns.
Laser or not? M+P Bodyguard 380 ACP

I have mixed feeling about lasers as sights, but I think they are very nice training aids, especially with a DA pistol like this one. Drop in a snap cap and squeeze that trigger over and over, until the laser stays in one place from beginning to end. Practice your draw stroke and get the laser on target early, and keep it on target as you extend your arms.

Do this a few hundred times and when you go back to the range you'll see the difference.

Great advice, I do this type of trigger training with my J-frame and I agree that it's a great training aid especially for heavy long stroke triggers. I hadn't, however, fully appreciated the value of the laser in training to get on target early in the draw stroke. I will opt for the gun with no laser to save weight, bulk and money, but I'll invest in something like this trigger guard laser to use for point/draw training. It's cheaper, and can be swapped out on all my guns for training. Thank you internet stranger, I think we made a good decision.

The main problem with the Bodyguard's laser is that you can't swap it out for a better one. If you're satisfied with the location and functions of its controls, and you're okay with its brightness, buy. Mind, the button on Bodyguard is set for your trigger finger, so you need other hand if you want push-and-hold.

BTW, pardon me asking, but why Bodyguard and not, say, Kahr or G42?
